messages.subject: MIMIC modelling for Informal Economy
parts:
Hi All,

 

I used the lavaan library to develop my MIMIC models to estimate Informal Economy values. I believe you may be familiar with the modelling, using a structural model to explain Informal Economy as a result of causal variables, and using a Measurement Model to have IE impacting some indicator variables.

 

Usually, MIMIC modelling for IE encompasses endogeneity, in the sense of having GPD variables as both causal and indicator variables.

 

On my modelling with MIMIC, I'm using inequality (GINI) as a causal variable. It's an endogenous variable, as inequality has impact on Informal Economy, and Informal Economy impacts inequality. The model was built this way on purpose, and my thesis is to show that the impact of inequality in Latin America is higher than in another sample of countries, e.g., worldwide sample.

 

MIMIC seemed to me the right tool to the modelling, exactly because of the way it's conceived.

 

Wanted to get your thoughts on it, as a reviewer of my article is questioning whether I shall use an endogenous variable on my MIMIC model. Literature has been using GDP as causal as well, and GDP is too endogenous.

 

Any light you may give me will be of help.

 

Thanks,

Marcos
